newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei end weak after breaching key support.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei end weak after breaching key support.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures tottered to their lowest close since May 1 on Tuesday as a long-standing support level finally gave way, triggering stop-loss sales in late trade, dealers said.
"Quite a number of stops were triggered below 19,500. We saw the market crash down to 19,410 in less than a minute," a trader at a large U.S. investment house said.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended 305 points easier at 20,450 after falling as low as 19,330. Volume was a hectic 28,300 lots.
"There was not much news but this was seen as a big support that broke," the trader said.
Dealers said an Economic Planning Agency report indicating continued weakness in housing construction and poor consumption data suggested Japan's economic recovery was still floundering.
Worries about a widening brokerage scandal after Yamaichi Securities revealed it had links with racketeers were also weighing on the market.
"The Nikkei managed a bit of a recovery on the cash side. But generally the feeling is that the economy is still weak," the trader said.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended 153.62 points down at 19,514.45 after hitting a low of 19,362.44.
Dealers said the September Nikkei could head lower, with the next support level seen at around 19,200/250.
Taiwan stock index futures finished sharply lower in line with Taipei stocks as tightening liquidity in the banking system spurred caution.
The MSCI August contract ended 9.3 lower at 414.4 on volume of 1,976 lots.
